title: Amends Charter: Portland residents decide 2% of city's annual discretionary budget.
ballot_label: Caption: Amends Charter: Portland residents decide 2% of city’s annual discretionary budget. Question: Should Portland create participatory budgeting program for residents to make binding decisions to spend 2% of city’s discretionary budget?
summary: A citizen-initiated Portland charter amendment requiring the City Council to allocate an amount equal to at least 2% of the city's adopted General Fund discretionary ongoing expenses to a participatory budgeting program. Residents could propose citywide or district projects; city staff and budget delegates would refine proposals, and residents would make binding selections. An oversight committee of residents would help develop the program, which would start July 2027.
yes_means: A yes vote amends the Portland City Charter to create a participatory budgeting program in which residents make binding decisions on spending an amount equal to at least 2% of the city's discretionary budget.
no_means: A no vote leaves the current budget process unchanged, in which the Mayor proposes and the Council amends and adopts the budget.
fiscal_impact: Under a recent forecast, the ballot summary gives a preliminary estimate of $16.4 million in FY 2027-28 and $17.0 million in FY 2028-29 to be allocated to the program; Council may identify funding from the entire city budget to meet the obligation.

arguments.author: Max Steele
arguments.statement: Max Steele's argument, printed under "Argument in Favor," is written in a sarcastic tone; it urges a yes vote and says the measure would likely create one of the largest participatory budgets in the country.
arguments.excerpt: You should vote yes on what is likely to be one of the largest participatory budgets in the country.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Nov 3, 2026 Voters' Pamphlet, p. M-79)

arguments.author: Tony Morse, Protect Our City Services
arguments.statement: Protect Our City Services cites a City Club of Portland report that described charter-mandated participatory budgeting as nearly unprecedented and difficult to justify from the available evidence.
arguments.excerpt: Proposals to adopt and institutionalize PB as a city-wide program funded through a charter change or citizen initiative appear to be nearly unprecedented in the U.S. and difficult to justify from the available evidence about PB’s benefits.

arguments.author: Bob Weinstein (with Mike Lindberg and Vadim Mozyrsky)
arguments.statement: Bob Weinstein, with Mike Lindberg and Vadim Mozyrsky, argues the charter amendment would require the city to direct at least 2% of discretionary spending, initially $16 million, to participatory budgeting.
arguments.excerpt: The proposal would amend Portland’s Charter to require the city to forever hand over at least 2% of discretionary spending — initially $16 million— to a participatory budgeting process, no matter what else the city needs.
